question:
Say that I have 2 models, where the second depends on the first. The first is an incremental model, while the second materializes as a table.

Is there a way to run/test/build the second model with the --full-refresh tag, so that the first incremental table is refreshed as well?

This is the command I'm running

clear && dbt run --full-refresh --select models/folder/my_model.sql+ --profiles-dir .

I've seen in the docs and elsewhere that adding the + at the end of the model path should cascade the full refresh, but i'm not seeing it actually happen. What can I do?
title: dbt trigger a full refresh that cascades downstream to all other models in the pipeline?
answer:
You were very close: the + operator works the following way: "If placed at the front of the model selector, + will select all parents of the selected model" (see docs https://docs.getdbt.com/reference/node-selection/graph-operators#the-plus-operator).

You are putting your operator at the end of your model name: models/folder/my_model.sql+

Meaning that you will only run all child models of my_model.

Therefore, I believe that placing the + operator in front, in order to run all parent models of my_model, would solve your issue:

dbt run --full-refresh --select +my_model --profiles-dir .

If you then also wanted to run all child models of my_model, you could place another + operator at the end:

dbt run --full-refresh --select +my_model+ --profiles-dir .
